sections.h2: Wheat's 1.0% rise was the smallest of the six rabi crops

chart.title: The other five rabi crops rose by 1.4% to 10.3%; wheat rose 1.0%
chart.sub: Rise in minimum support price, 2027-28 over 2026-27, %.

sections.means: Wheat's support price rose by Rs 25 a quintal, the smallest percentage rise of the six rabi crops.
sections.todo: Compare the 1.0% wheat rise with the 5.6% to 10.3% rises for oilseeds and pulses when judging which crops farmers will sow.

sections.h2: Wheat's margin over cost is 106%, the widest of the six crops

chart.title: Wheat still earns the widest margin over cost, at 106%
chart.sub: Government's margin over the all-India weighted average cost of production, %.

sections.means: Even after the small rise, wheat's margin of 106% is the widest of the six rabi crops.
sections.todo: Watch whether the oilseed and pulse rises narrow the margin gap with wheat in the next season's support prices.

sections.h2: Wheat stock on 1 September was 2.3 times the buffer norm

chart.title: Rice stock was 3.8 times its norm, wheat 2.3 times
chart.sub: Central pool stock on 1 September 2026 as a multiple of the 1 October buffer norm.
chart.source: Food Corporation of India figures, as reported.
rows: 479.92 lakh tonnes against a norm of 205.2
390.53 lakh tonnes against a norm of 102.5

sections.means: The central pool held 479.92 lakh tonnes of wheat on 1 September 2026, against a buffer norm of 205.2 lakh tonnes.
sections.todo: Hold any large support price rise until wheat stocks fall back towards the buffer norm, since a big rise would add to stocks the government is already trying to sell.
